title: Trump’s attempt to rename AI is looking awfully artificial
slides: The new name leans ideological, not technical
Even his allies hesitate to repeat it
Global labs won't adopt Washington's label
Watch what Washington funds, not what it calls it
thread_text:
1. Trump's AI rebrand

The White House pushed a name change for AI that has nothing to do with technology — and everything to do with politics. It's already dividing the industry.

2. Ideology, not engineering

The new label signals a worldview, not a capability. That's why it doesn't appear in any technical standard or research paper.

3. Allies won't say it

Even close political partners are avoiding the phrase in public. Behind closed doors, they worry it ties them to a narrative they can't control.

4. The world ignores it

Labs in Europe and Asia won't adopt Washington's branding. They'll keep using 'AI' — and competing on results, not rhetoric.

5. Follow the money, not the name

Check where US AI research grants actually go next quarter. If you want to know what Washington really thinks, read the budget, not the speech.

instagram.caption:
Washington wants to rebrand AI with a political label — and even Trump's own allies won't repeat it in public. 🤔

The new name signals ideology, not capability, so it appears in no technical standard or research paper.

Labs in Europe and Asia keep calling it AI, competing on results instead of rhetoric.

If you use AI tools daily, nothing changes yet — same models, same APIs. What shifts is how Washington funds research, and that budget lands next quarter. 📊

Check where US AI grants go in the next three months: does the naming affect funding, or just the speeches? 👀
